gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.

gaps.sentence: The assistant ___ I spoke to was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after a preposition-style clause.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: He is a colleague on ___ you can always depend.
gaps.explanation: After 'on', the formal relative pronoun for a person is 'whom'.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ produces these parts has factories in three countries.
gaps.explanation: A company takes 'which' as subject; 'who' is normally reserved for individual people.
